speaker: Enzo Maresca
quote_text:
Peter. Enzo, you must be pleased with  the scoreline, but also it seems,  
I don't know if you'll clarify, that everyone  emerged unscathed in terms of injuries as well.  
Yeah, as you said, first of all, very happy  with the result, with the performance. It's  
European competition semi-final, so it's very  important. Again, we plan the game in one way  
at the beginning and to finish in a different  way. I think that the performance for one hour,  
70 minutes was a good performance. Then we dropped  a little bit, the last 15, 20 minutes, probably  
because we were 0-3, 0-4, but that showed that  we cannot allow ourselves to drop because it's  
always complicated. And yeah, the message is that  against Warsaw away, we won 0-3, but then at home  
we struggled. So it's a good experience and for  sure, the next leg at home, we're going to finish  
our job and hopefully we can reach the final. So,  for you, the tie is still not say again? The tie  
is not done, it feels you still feel the tie  is still alive? The round, the semi-final,  
it's not over. Oh, no, no, absolutely. We have  the experience from Warsaw that we won there 0-3  
and then at home we struggled. So that it's a good  experience because we can learn from that. So, we  
need to finish the job at home. Hi Enzo, what was  the thinking about giving Reggie Walsh's debut?  
It must have been a great moment. He's very young.  To be honest, it's already a long time that I feel  
excited to give him the debut chance because it's  so good. He's very young, but in the way we want  
to play, in our way, in our style, it's perfect.  But he's still very young. He needs to learn,  
he needs to work hard and he needs to grow for  sure. But we are happy. They just said to me that  
we gave 8 debuts this season from the academy.  I think it's good. Are his mum and dad angry at  
you because he's probably got school and exams and  stuff coming up? This is the most important thing  
for him in this moment, no doubt. Thank you. Ben.  Just following on, there's a lovely picture of you  
whispering something into Reggie's ear just before  he came on. He's got a big smile on his face. What  
did you say to him? No, just to enjoy the moment,  be happy, playing the way he's training with us  
every day. So this was my message because in some  days of the season, he worked with us. And he's  
so good because he makes everything easy. And as I  said, but he's very young and he needs to continue  
to work. And just a word on Nicolas Jackson,  two goals. The second one was a superb finish.  
Yeah, but Nico scored against Everton. So  it's all about confidence. You see now that he  
looks a different player from weeks ago. Hopefully  the same thing is going to happen with Cole. It's  
just a matter to, you know, break that moment and  go again. Simon. Enzo, leisure home game aside,  
how much do you think the Conference League,  you talked last night about winning mentality,  
how much do you think it's helping bring you guys  back into form, players back in confidence, we're  
seeing Jadon Sancho score, Nicolas Jackson and  so on and so forth, that it's creating a positive  
vibe which can also take into the Premier League.  Yeah, yeah, absolutely. But if you remember the  
game at home against Warsaw, we start with Nicolas  and Cole from the beginning and both struggled.  
Now you can see that Nico looks a bit different  player, but because he scored against Everton,  
now he has again confidence and we know how good  is Nico for us. The same thing is absolutely for  
Cole and hopefully we can have also him, you  know, scoring goal and assist very soon. And  
just a quick one. Nottingham Forest, you know,  lost tonight. Does this make it a perfect night  
for you and Chelsea? We were focused on our game.  That was the priority for us. Then after the game,  
for sure, they mentioned me about also Forest.  But I think we need to be focused on us. And  
this is the most important thing. Rob. Hi Enzo.  Noni Madueke, you were quite critical of earlier  
in the season in terms of his attitude, some of  what he was doing in training and in matches.  
Do you feel like you've had the response from him  that you wanted and he's now doing consistently  
what you expect from him, both in terms of  his performance and his attitude? Absolutely,  
yes. Absolutely. Noni is the reason why I try to  push Noni is because I think he can do better and  
better and better. So this is the only reason why.  In terms of numbers, I think he scored in all the  
competitions more than ten goals. Also, with  that, so in terms of numbers, his season has  
been very good, but hopefully we are still at the  moment five more games, 4 Premier League games,  
plus the second leg. Hopefully, in the next five  games, he can help us with some more goals. We'll  
do two more questions. They have them in the  middle, please. Hi, I was just wondering what you  
thought about the atmosphere tonight and if you  had to compare it to the atmosphere you're used to  
in the Premier League, how would you rate it? No,  yeah, the environment was very nice, very good. I  
said to the players that they are lucky to play  this kind of games with this environment. I said  
yesterday that the same environment was in Poland  when we played against Warsaw, so it's nice and we  
have also a good environment in England. Hiya. So,  what do you think of Djurgården and specifically  
Isak Alemayehu Mulugeta's performance tonight? I  think, as I said yesterday, it's quite clear what  
they want to do on the ball, what they want to do  off the ball. I think tonight we were very good,  
don't allow them to play. We were very aggressive.  We were, like always, trying to be aggressive,  
man-to-man, high pressing, and probably we were  quite strong in our first pressing and they  
struggled a little bit to build. But at the  same time, in some moments, you can see that  
they are dangerous and they have some very  good players. Okay, thanks everyone. Thank you.
title: Enzo Maresca post-match press conference | Djurgarden 1-4 Chelsea | Europa Conference League
